428.t: Local Philadelphia bands and Les Robinson at the Club Harlem
428.s: He lists his local bands 1933-35, the Les Robinson group, its members, and playing Cab Calloway and Ellington hits when they came to listen.
428.ch: Philadelphia bands and the Club Harlem
428.q: We had the best bands in Philly. Jimmy Shine's Jungle Band, you know, had those odd names. Les Robinson's band, which was the band that I -- the last band that I played with, [1936] 1935. Bessie Smith, that was her last engagement before she went South and got in the automobile accident.

428.t: Bill Doggett's big band in Philadelphia
428.s: Hall describes the arranged ensemble band with Shadow Wilson on drums and how he brought Philadelphia friends to New York.
428.ch: New York arrival, Billy Hicks and the Black Cat
428.q: That's right, and then prior to that I had been working with Bill Doggett in Philadelphia and we had a big band, Shadow Wilson was the drummer.

428.t: Bill Doggett's Philadelphia big band (second pass)
428.s: Repeat of the Doggett band and Hall bringing Philadelphians to New York.
428.ch: New York 1936-39 (second pass of the transcript)
428.q: Yeah. And prior to that I had been working with Bill Dawgett in Philadelphia and we had a big band, Shadow Wilson was the drummer.

70.s: He moves to Zack White's band, with Si Oliver as arranger, a good band but outplayed by Speed Webb.
70.ch: Childhood and first bands in Ohio
70.q: And he played the trumpet then. He was playing the trumpet in the band. It was a nice little band. There was a lot of bands out there in the West, though, that to me that -- you know, someone could play it better, like Speed Webb. Speed Webb came to the Paradise Ballroom in Cincinnati and made us…

70.t: The septet at Manitou Beach, Goldkette and the Cottonpickers name (repeat)
70.s: Jackson retells how Goldkette heard the seven-piece band at Clark's Lake, had Redman enlarge it, and gave it the Cotton Pickers name and Victor contract in 1927.
70.ch: Musicians of the era: players, drummers, bassists, pianists
70.q: Seven pieces, and they used to play up to Manitou Beach, Michigan, every summer. The guys would get out of school and they'd go up there and play.

75.t: Alex Hill and "Long About Midnight" with Willie Bryant
75.s: He met Hill with Bryant in Philadelphia in 1935; the song was Willie's Apollo feature.
75.ch: Recent years and early piano influences
75.q: "Long About Midnight." That was Willie's big song at the Apollo Theatre. We were the house band at the Apollo Theatre, you see...

75.t: Billy Hicks and the Sizzling Six
75.s: Billy Hicks's band was the first local Black band at the St. Regis; earlier, around 1931-32, he took a band to Haiti.
75.ch: The war years: Barnet, Hot Lips Page, Newton and Kirby
75.q: band to play St. Regis. I was in Europe when that happened. But prior to that, it was back in the Thirties, the early Thirties, about '31 or '32, Billy Hicks, Joe Vidas(?), Quinton Harrington and...

243.t: Bill Phillips's Syncopators and other local bands
243.s: The High Hatters turned into Bill Phillips's band, after which Breaux worked with nearly every local band, including Robichaux, Barbarin and Kid Howard.
243.q: Alfred, uh, Alfred plays saxophone with Skiz play bass. He's up around, out around Naptown, Indianapolis somewhere now. Final bass player too. Very nice. And, uh, well, I went on with them with the Preston City high-hats. And I stayed with them until, uh, oh, I guess we kept the band going until,…

462.s: He was on the road with Bob Chester before Woody Herman, took up lead alto in Buddy Williams's Philadelphia band, and played Dayton broadcasts on WLW.
462.ch: Early bands and the swing era

367.s: Carter's last job was a battle against an Alabama college band in Dayton; Gerald Wilson then left for Lunceford, and Young assesses his playing.
367.q: Well, Chick Carter‘s band, I played with Chick Carter‘s band and Gerald got in, Gerald Wilson got in Chick Carter‘s band. We was in Dayton and we played a battle of jazz against…

109.t: Why the band is called Jeter-Pillars
109.s: The band was named for altoist Jimmy Jeter and tenorist Charles Pillars, and was the house band at the Plantation with several broadcasts a week.
109.q: Oh, it was a fantastic band. They used to do -- oh, we had at least four or five broadcasts a week out of the Plantation.

383.t: Joining Speed Webb's band in Muncie
383.s: Speed Webb, riding on a movie appearance, takes Wilson, Gus and Roy Eldridge to Muncie and assembles a band including Vic Dickenson and Reunald Jones.
383.q: So a guy named Speed Webb came to town, to Detroit, and I guess this was still in 1929, late in the year, and he had just made a movie called On With the Show, where he was a bandleader in that, and the star of that was Ethel Waters.

170.t: Philadelphia in 1961 with Al Gray and Billy Mitchell
170.s: Ware plays a week at Pep's and a TV show with the Al Gray-Billy Mitchell sextet.
170.q: I came down here -- I think it was '61 -- with Al Gray and Billy Mitchell. They had a sextet. We had a week at Peps, old Peps down there on Broad Street. He had a trumpet player -- I forgot the brother's name -- he also had arranger, Gene, who played piano as well as peck horn. That's an alto horn,…

31.t: Directing for the Nicholas Brothers in Philadelphia
31.s: Whaley retells how he was told to direct the band for the Nicholas Brothers before he had ever directed.
31.ch: Reel IV retellings and New York pianists
31.q: Now the Nicholas Brothers -- they came after them, but I was directing a band over in Philadelphia, see, and the man comes to me and says -- no, I was playing piano, I also played piano, and he asked me why didn't I direct the band and let this woman -- and he was talking about Mrs. Nicholas, she…

124.t: Lil Armstrong's band at the Vendome Hotel in Buffalo
124.s: McRae joined Lil Armstrong's band in Buffalo, where he met the Will Mastin Trio, then played the Harlem Theater in New York.
124.ch: Depression gigs, Lil Armstrong, joining Chick Webb
124.q: And Lil Armstrong was gigging, and Charlie Green said she wanted to work. So Charlie Green bought her that band -- Stuff Smith's band. Stuff got a small band. Jonah Jones and all the guys was in that band. (Inaudible) Stuff Smith's band.

86.t: Heat Wave Bar band and Slim Waters on tuba
86.s: Edison lists the small Jeter-Pillars lineup at the Heat Wave Bar and long hours, plus guitarist Jimmy Miller who married Catherine.
86.ch: Jeter-Pillars in Cleveland and St. Louis
86.q: Cleveland, yeah. And then we started working a place that was just a hotel, called the Heat Wave Bar. This was Jester-Pillars, I was playing trumpet, Snub Mosley was playing trombone and Godley was playing drums. I forget who we had on bass. A guy playing tuba named Slim Waters. He could play tuba…

473.t: Stuff Smith's band stranded in Philadelphia and taken over by Lil Armstrong
473.s: The band played the Lafayette in New York and the Lincoln in Philadelphia, got stranded, was joined by Teddy McRae, and then Lil Armstrong took over the band, Stuff excluded.
473.ch: Buffalo, Lunceford, Lil Armstrong and Stuff Smith
473.q: York, we had George Clark and two altos, George on tenor and two alto players. Good altos, and clarinet. And we go to -- into the Lafayette. See the Apollo wasn't open in '32, and then we go from there to the Lincoln Theater in Philadelphia, and things didn't work out too good, we're stranded…
